title: SplitInboxLayout
wrapsNative: NavigationSplitView(sidebar:detail:) with List(selection:) for the list and detail panes, and inspector(isPresented:content:) for the context pane; NavigationSplitView(sidebar:content:detail:) when the list has folders
summary: An inbox is the system's split view: the list and the detail are NavigationSplitView columns, and the context pane is an inspector. On iPhone one pane shows at a time with back navigation. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a list of items opened one at a time with extra context, such as a support inbox, mail or a queue of approvals.
whenNotToUse: For a list without a detail pane, use a List in a NavigationStack. For two panes only, see split-layout.

states.name: compact width
states.description: One pane at a time: the list, then the detail with a back button; the inspector is a sheet.

states.name: regular width
states.description: The list and the detail side by side; the inspector is a column at the trailing edge.

states.name: nothing selected
states.description: The detail shows an empty state.

states.name: context hidden
states.description: The toolbar button shows and hides the inspector.

appearance: System columns, separators and selection; the selection takes the accent through the tint. Rows, the empty state and the context content are Monarch components.
platformNotes: The parity map named a three-column NavigationSplitView. The web's three panes are list, detail and context; on iOS the context pane is an inspector, which the system shows as a trailing column on iPad and as a sheet on iPhone, while the three-column NavigationSplitView is for a folder sidebar before the list, shown in the second example. The web's breakpoints, pane toggles, resizing, focus management and list collapse are the system's: columnVisibility collapses the list, and inspectorColumnWidth sizes the context pane. Android uses the Material list-detail scaffold.
accessibility: System behaviour: the list is a list with selection, columns are separate containers for VoiceOver, and the back button returns to the list on iPhone.
The inspector toggle is a toolbar button whose label says what it does.
Selection is shown by the system highlight and the selected trait, not colour alone.
edgeCases: Keep the selection in state that survives size changes, so rotating an iPad does not lose the open item.
inspector needs iOS 17, the deployment target.
On iPhone the inspector is a sheet; give it presentationDetents if it is short.

examples.template:
HStack(spacing: 0) {
    list
        .frame(width: theme.spacing.space24 * 1.7)
    Rectangle().fill(theme.colors.borderSubtle).frame(width: 1)
    conversation
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)
}
.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous))
.overlay(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous).stroke(theme.colors.borderSubtle, lineWidth: 1))
.frame(height: theme.spacing.space24 * 4.4)
